short: A small cash float for minor day-to-day payments.
seoTitle: Petty Cash — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Petty cash is a small float of physical cash kept for minor expenses — auto fare, courier charges, a last-minute purchase.
definition: Petty cash is a small float of physical cash kept for minor expenses — auto fare, courier charges, a last-minute purchase. It is usually run on an imprest system, topped back up to a fixed amount.
bodyHtml:
Why Petty Cash matters

Petty cash is small enough to be ignored and leaky enough to matter. Unvouchered spending accumulates quietly and is the hardest category to reconstruct at year end.

Petty Cash formula

Cash on hand + Vouchers held = Imprest float

Any shortfall is an unrecorded payment.

How Petty Cash works in practice

Fix the float, require a voucher for every payment, and reimburse only against vouchers so the box always totals cash plus vouchers. Count it weekly, by someone who does not hold the key.

faq.question: How much petty cash should I hold?
faq.answer: About two weeks of small expenses — enough to avoid constant top-ups, small enough to limit exposure.

faq.question: Who should hold petty cash?
faq.answer: One named person, with counts done by someone else. Separating custody from checking is the whole control.
